_comment: OPT-IN ruleset — not applied by apply.sh, and not part of the default set.
Requires every commit pushed to main to carry a verified GPG or SSH
signature. It is the one rule in this directory that asks something of a
contributor beyond 'open a pull request', which is exactly why it is opt-in:
a student's first contribution should not fail on a key they have not set up.
Apply with:
bash .github/branch-protection/apply.sh --file optional/require-signed-commits.json
BEFORE YOU DO
1. Every maintainer must sign:
git config --global user.signingkey <key>
git config --global commit.gpgsign true
(SSH signing: gpg.format=ssh, user.signingkey=~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub)
2. Check the history is already signed. An unsigned commit that is reachable
from main does not need re-signing to keep the rule green, but the next
push of that commit does — verify with:
git log --format='%h %G? %s' -20 main
and expect 'G' (good) rather than 'N' (none).
3. Remember that a squash merge is signed by GitHub, not by the author, so
the squash-merge workflow keeps working. It is direct pushes and the
commits inside a pull request that must carry a signature.
Removing it later is the same command with --remove --file, so this is
reversible in about ten seconds.
name: Require signed commits
